impact_scope.description: S1 adds a new public Handsum image-decoder entry surface implementing base.image_decoder; no corresponding production file or declaration exists in S0.
The new decoder exposes a caller-driven call-sequence protocol through states 0x00, 0x20, 0x28, 0x40, and 0x60.
S1 introduces Handsum-format input handling, including its magic header, version/aspect byte, truncation behavior, source reader, destination pixel buffer, blend mode, and work buffer arguments.

evidence: S0 has no std/handsum/decode_handsum.wuffs file and the selected S0 context reports no matching declaration.
Because the Handsum decoder entry surface and format do not exist in S0, H0 has no Handsum-specific exposure or controllability obligation in S0.

gap_after.type: missing exposure of new decoder, format, and call protocol
evidence: S1 adds the public Handsum decoder and its image-config, frame-config, frame-decoding, and restart calls.
H0 enables and exercises only BASE, JSON, AUX__BASE, and AUX__JSON modules and invokes JSON decoding paths; it neither enables nor instantiates the Handsum decoder.
H0 cannot construct Handsum input or control the new decoder's configuration/frame/restart call sequence and caller-supplied image-decoding arguments.

new_harness_obligation.description: A harness must compile/enable the new Handsum module, construct Handsum byte input, instantiate its decoder, and drive the image-config/frame-config/frame-decoding protocol with appropriate destination pixel-buffer and other caller-supplied arguments; none of these actions was needed in S0.
evidence: The production file and decoder interface are wholly new in S1.
The decoder's public methods require a source reader and, for frame decoding, a destination pixel buffer, blend value, work buffer, and options pointer.
The unchanged JSON H0 contains no Handsum module selection, decoder call, image buffer construction, or Handsum call-order transitions.

reason: Within the stable scope of the newly introduced Handsum decoder, S0 has no harness gap because the surface does not exist, while S1 has a material exposure and controllability gap because H0 remains JSON-only. The commit therefore creates concrete compile-time, input-construction, caller-argument, and call-order obligations, yielding NEW.
